title: RUNNER.md rule 2 unconditionally requires a reproduction rule in the public run issue — needs the access-control carve-out at the source
body:
Docs-only, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/RUNNER.md`. Follow-up from PR #9470 (skills card #9387), which identified this residual and correctly could not fix it — its file surface excludes `docs/qa/**`.

## The conflict, verified on `main` (`ad217b192`)

`RUNNER.md:55` reads, with no exception:

> A `fail` with no reproduction rule in its issue is not a completed verdict.

The `checklist-test` skill is gaining a guardrail (PR #9470, awaiting maintainer review) that forbids publishing a reproduction for an authentication or authorization hole **anywhere on GitHub**, and which has to state that it *overrides* this sentence to work at all.

So after #9470 lands, two documents a runner is told to obey disagree, and the conflict is resolved only by **precedence asserted from one side**. That is the shape that rots: the next person to read RUNNER.md on its own gets the unconditional rule and no hint that a carve-out exists.

## Why this is not cosmetic

This exact conflict already caused a real disclosure. In wave #9296 a runner found an unauthenticated read/write hole, followed the protocol faithfully, and published a working reproduction — because the protocol **told it to**. The instruction it received (withhold from the run issue, post to the tracking card) was the PM's error, but the underlying pull came from here: rule 2 makes a reproduction rule the definition of a completed `fail` verdict, so a runner suppressing one believes it is filing an incomplete verdict.

A runner should not have to choose between "complete verdict" and "do not publish an exploit". Rule 2 should say so itself.

## Scope

Add the carve-out to rule 2 in place — a `fail` on an authentication or authorization clause is complete **without** a published reproduction, provided it records the item, the clause, and that the detail is withheld pending the maintainer, with the reproduction held by the runner. Keep it short; rule 2's force for every other failure class must not soften.

Worth checking while in the file: the trap vocabulary and the "Environment facts" section (extended by #9427) for any other unconditional phrasing that assumes every finding is safe to publish.

⛔ No `.claude/skills/**` in this PR — #9470 owns the skill side and is awaiting a human merge; touching both would drag this docs-only change into the same queue.
